utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, I should just like you to explain something to me. This is the list of witness order provided to me by the opposite side, and the time provided, three hours. You explained yesterday that that applies to me too and that that is together. So can you tell me whether the opposite side is now limiting the time I have for my cross-examination too, or is that your job?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. That reference to time is purely an estimate which the Prosecution make as to the time which a witness is likely to take. It's not binding on anybody. It's merely a forecast. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Very well. But I assume that you're bearing in mind the fact that this witness was the president of the Party of Democratic Action in Bratunac, and you also heard from the previous witness, who was a protected witness, that in that municipality, except two, all the other Serb villages were razed to the ground and the inhabitants that weren't able to escape were killed. So I don't see why I shouldn't have a little more time to question this witness. He must have known about these events.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You can ask him about them now. We have in fact considered all these matters in setting the time available. Now, let us move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you're not going to give me more time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let's move on. Yes. We'll hear an application at the end, but start the cross-examination now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Milosevic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Gusic, yesterday during your testimony, you said that all the posts of leadership in the Bratunac municipality by and large were held by the Serbs, and you even went on to quote about 80 per cent, I believe. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was speaking about the public services, public enterprises in the Bratunac municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Public, socially owned, whatever you like to call them, all of them together. But is it true that the director of the company called Vihor was Djordje Sead? Just give me yes or no answers, please, to save time.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was an economic commercial enterprise. What I was talking about was not commercial enterprises. As far as commercial enterprises, there were directors who were Muslims and Serbs alike.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, all right. Is it true then that Faho Djodjic was the director of the Kaolin factory?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it true that Mujo Mujcic, another man, was director of the ceramics factory in Bratunac? Is that also true?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think for a time, yes. I don't know when exactly. But you're talking about commercial enterprises. I was talking about the social services companies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Edo Ahmic was he the director of Kartonaza?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Cazim Avdic, a director of Feros company?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Feros company was not located in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Enver Hekic? Was he the director of the Autotransport company?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it true that Rifat Besic was director of the timber industry in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rifat Besic died several years before the occupation of Bratunac took place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it true that Ahmic Selmanagic were director and deputy director of the Sase mine?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Sase mine is not located in Bratunac. It is the Srebrenica municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that the director of the secondary school in Bratunac was also a Muslim by the name of Hasib Hasanovic?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And primary school, Taib Avdic, also a Muslim? Is that true too?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about the primary school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How come you don't know?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. There may be things that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, it's such a small place and you were the president of the party. I assume you ought to know.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Taib Avdic, the name doesn't ring a bell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You don't know him. And president of the court for misdemeanors, was he Bahret Kustura?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was at one time president of the misdemeanors court, but of late he worked as an inspector in the municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Hajro Halilovic, president of another court?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bratunac did not have a first instance court.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, he was in the area of one first instance court and the president was Hajro Halilovic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hajro Halilovic, as far as I know, was the president of the first instance court in the Srebrenica municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did that first instance court cover Bratunac too?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that's what I'm talking about. So what kind of Serb domination in Bratunac are you speaking about at all if all this is correct, what I have put to you?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You enumerated just a number of directorship posts, and you have a lot of misinformation there. You were wrong on many counts. I was talking about social companies in the social services and you were talking about commercial enterprises.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, these are all socially owned companies.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But they also engaged in the private sector.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Mujo Zukic, was he president of the Municipal Assembly? Is that true?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the first party elections were held and when the government was constituted --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just give me a yes or no answer. Was he or wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ljubicic was president of the Municipal Assembly of Bratunac and the Executive Board president was Djukanovic and these were parallel posts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it true that the chief of police in Bratunac was Senad Hadzic?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Senad Hodzic was elected as chief of police at the end of the 1991, and the commander of the police force --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about the commander. I'm asking you about this other man. Is it true that the head of the municipal department for national defence was Dzemail Becirevic?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We already established yesterday that the chief of staff for Territorial Defence was Safet Mujkic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not Safet Mujkic, not at that time, he wasn't the commander of the TO staff. I told you that yesterday. He was at some time before the commander of the Territorial Defence Staff but not during that period of time. Safet Mujkic was not territorial commander at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was, then? Who was it?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Dzemo Hodzic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is Dzemo Hodzic a Muslim too?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I answered that question yesterday and said he was, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now, as you're saying there was absolutely no cause and that on the 17th of April although there was no fighting certain forces were in Bratunac. Mr. Gusic, are you aware of the fact that on the 14th of April, that is to say several days prior to that, a column of cadets from Rajlovac near Sarajevo, which was withdrawing with its weapons and materiel through the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina, in keeping with the federal government, was attacked in the village of Hranca, this column of cadets. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is absolutely not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know that there was shooting from an ambush attacking the column of cadets from Rajlovac and that many of them were seriously wounded and injured and all the rest of it?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I do apologise, but I have to say that that is pure fabrication.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, people are watching these proceedings from Bratunac and will be able to assess themselves which of the two of us are telling the truth, you or I.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course we are being watched, the proceedings are being watched, and I have taken the solemn declaration to tell the truth and I stand by each word I utter and I'm ready to be held accountable.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know about the brothers Ramic from Bratunac? Have you heard of them, Abdurahman and two others? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know what Nezir Ramic's sons are called from Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know of the Hadzic brothers from Hranca and Redzo Arifovic and his brother Zoka? Have you heard of them?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I really haven't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, according to my information, all these were individuals who organised the ambush of the cadets column from Rajlovac and the shooting that took place when they were shot at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You know quite well you are not to put something which the witness denies happened. It's a complete waste of time to go on putting the same thing. Now, we have considered your application for more time. We will give you a total of 35 minutes this morning, which gives you a quarter of an hour extra. But you won't get any extra time if you waste it by putting the same things over and over again.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. I'm not repeating the same things, Mr. May.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But do you know that it was the JNA's task to prevent conflicts and attacks, first and foremost to protect the units of the JNA which were withdrawing from Bosnia and to disarm the Muslims and Serbs and to prevent conflicts between the two?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That observation of yours is not correct. It was the task of the Yugoslav People's Army in concrete terms in the Bratunac municipality was to arm the Serb population in Bratunac and to lay down all the necessary preparations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you answer my questions, please. Have you heard of Ejub Golic?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've heard of the name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear that he was from the village of Glogova, from the Bratunac municipality? Just yes or no.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that at the end of 1991, he organised barricades, roadblocks, and the local police-controlled checkpoints at which they would stop Serbs and mistreat them?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know about that. And is it true that later on he became the commander of the infamous battalion of the 28th Division from Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about this. I was in an encirclement in Bratunac in Glogova, Srebrenica, from the 17th of April. On the 17th of April, I left Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm talking about the end of 1991 and the Mountain Brigade.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't think anybody was involved.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you yourself from the 17th of April onwards then?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the 17th of April onwards, for a time I was in Gradacac, and then I was in Banovici, and then in Tuzla, and Kladanj, and so on. That's where I stayed for a time and was on assignment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But I'm sure you were interested about what was going on in Bratunac in the meantime and you followed all the events taking place there.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course I was interested in that. And as far as I was able, I did always like to get news from Bratunac to see what was going on. That's quite normal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Gusic. Yesterday you claimed here that as an activist of the SDA and one of the vice-presidents, you knew nothing about the existence of any kind of Muslim armed formations in the Bratunac area in the period between 1991 up until your departure; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is right. They did not exist on the territory of Bratunac. No kind of Muslim formation existed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also said you knew nothing about the existence of the so-called, and can I call it infamous, Patriotic League of Nations in the Bratunac municipality in 1991 and 1992 and its units; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you're calling it the Patriotic League. I think that as regards those activities, it's not even worth mentioning in view of the fact that Bratunac was a peaceful place, calm place, which offered in resistance on the 17th of April. Not a single bullet was shot by a Muslim at all which would merit ethnic cleansing on the part of Serb formations after the 17th of April, the killing thousands of Muslim civilians, men, military-able men, elderly men, women, children, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday we noted that nobody fired a single bullet on the 17th of April. Now, do you know the name of Nijaz Masic at all?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that name. It does ring a bell, sounds familiar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he write a booklet of some kind about Bratunac which was published in 1996? Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nijaz Masic was an historian and he always collected information and data, and yes, he did write a book about Bratunac, a leaflet about Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the introduction to his book, in the preface, it says that during his work, he consulted all important commanders of units and representatives of political and state bodies of the Bratunac municipality. And then he goes on to say and that he would like to express his gratitude to Professor Dr. Tarik Kulenovic especially, Dzevad Gusic as well, that is to say to you, Gusic, and Sabic and professor Ibrahim Tepic. So he expresses his thanks to four people, amongst whom is your name. I assume you know that.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Tell me, then, in that book, as an historian, he states the following: With his -- its party line, the Party of Democratic Action from the beginning of September 1991 organised village guards, village watches. Is that true? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as the village watches --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just say yes or no, please. Give me a yes or no answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Don't interrupt the witness like that. You mustn't harry him.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'd be very grateful to you, Mr. May, if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Now, don't interrupt, and let the witness answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We've got no translation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you hear the English on this channel? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yesterday, I said during my statement that there was controlled night shooting from Serb villages against Muslim villages. This went on for days and days. So the locals from these villages, the Muslims from Muslim villages, organised village guards because they were terribly frightened and worried about everything that was going on. So that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Since it's correct, then he says the following: "The delegation of the SDA of Bratunac consisting of Nijaz Dubicic, Sabit Mujkic, Azem Dzanic, and Dzemail Becirevic took part in the meeting of the initiative committee of the communities from the Drina area in order to establish the Patriotic League of the Tuzla district held on the 16th of July, 1991 in Srebrenica. That meeting is well-known under the name of the Drina Region Initiative." So in July 1991, you established a Patriotic League, and this Drina Region Initiative is referred to here. And you say that you know nothing about the organisation of the Patriotic League in your area, although this man thanks you for the -- for having consulted him in the preparation of this book.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, see, as far as acknowledgments are concerned, I did give a contribution, I did talk to the distinguished Professor Nijaz Masic, and I told him about certain political activities and political developments. That is to say in relation to this particular period in Bratunac before the war and up to the 17th of April. And now as for this allegation that you're making or, rather, what you've read allegedly from this book, I don't know whether this is exactly what it says in the book, but if it is what it says, then it is probably the author's right to write something like that on the basis of some information. I would not like to go into this. Perhaps he should be asked about this. But what I would like to tell you for sure is what I know myself. At that time, we from the Party of Democratic Action did have information, that is to say verified information, that the Yugoslav People's Army and the Serb Democratic Party were arming the Serb people and that they were carrying out preparations among the Serb people for a possible war. We had information that the Serb Democratic Party --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking you that, sir.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- established a Crisis Staff for the municipality of Bratunac and for all the local communes. We had information that constant intimidation was going on against the Muslim people, and we also had several cases of beatings --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Gusic, we've heard that, I think. If you'd just concentrate on the accused's questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really am sorry. I felt it was necessary for me to say this in order to clarify the following: As the committee of the SDA, we had requests coming from people stating that we should organise ourselves to defend Bratunac or, rather, against an attempt to occupy Bratunac by Serb formations and by the Yugoslav People's Army from Serbia. So it is under these circumstances, under such circumstances that I've just described we from the SDA charged a certain person with particular duties. We gave him a free hand in order to organise defence in Bratunac against a possible occupation of the municipality. And I have to say with regret that this was never successful. This person tried to talk to people in the area --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I hope that you are really going to cut this short, this speech of yours over here.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. I'm going to try to cut it short. So we charged Sabit Mujkic with this. We already discussed this yesterday. And in view of this danger and in view of the great danger involved, all of this happened before 10 -- I mean, everybody who could, left Bratunac ten days before the occupation of Bratunac took place, whenever they could. So it wasn't really that much was done in this particular field.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that's what you're saying now, but what it says here, what is written here is that the president of the municipality and Sabit Mujkic, as commander of the Territorial Defence of Bratunac, was at a meeting at the 11th -- on the 11th of January 1991 in Tolsic, in the municipality of Kalesija and, at the request of the Bratunac delegation, a decision was passed to send Samir Nisovic to Bratunac to coordinate the work of the Patriotic League of Bratunac. So a Patriotic League of Bratunac was already established, and he, on the 11th of January, got the assignment to coordinate the work of the Patriotic League of Bratunac. Is that correct or is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the establishment of the Patriotic League, it was never established in the municipality of Bratunac. An attempt was made to have something done, but it failed and it was for the reasons that I already referred to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it says here Samir Nisovic, and I mean I'm just quoting what is written in this book, immediately started carrying out this assignment. He arrived in Bratunac. First the SDA of Bratunac in 1991 established a Patriotic League for Bratunac while its military establishment was carried out in February 1992. That's what it says here. He has helped the military establishment of the Patriotic League and it was indeed established under the auspices of the SDA of Bratunac in February of 1992 in Voljevica at the premises of the local commune of Voljevica. So that is what is written here in his book, and he thanks you for the consultations he carried out with you. So is this correct or is this not correct? Just tell me that.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm really going to give you a precise answer now. I think that this should get over with. When I became party president on the 21st of March 1992, there was no Patriotic League. Nothing had been done in concrete terms for this Patriotic League to be able to function in this area. There were only attempts that had been made, just attempts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So your answer to this question of mine is that what this man has written here is incorrect.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct to the effect that an attempt was made to have something done.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But he's not writing about an attempt. So you are saying that this is not correct.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, historians probably have information of their own, they have their own reasons for writing things, and I wouldn't like to go into all of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But he says the Patriotic League of Bratunac decided that the Patriotic League Staff should consist of people who had certain military skills, and then he enumerates some names. So you know nothing about this and all this was just an attempt?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of this was just an attempt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. It says here that in most of the free territory, the municipality of Bratunac in Konjevic Polje a War Presidency was established with the most political prominent representatives of all parts and links were established and agreement was given to establish a War Presidency of the municipality of Bratunac as a political organ of government, and one of the most important decisions reached was the establishment of a municipal Crisis Staff of the municipality of Bratunac and Velid Sabic was appointed as commander. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, could you tell me first what are the dates involved specifically.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, this War Presidency is the 16th of July, 1992, and I can see that you know very well what this is all about.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this was carried out when the occupation of Bratunac was carried out, when the ethic cleansing of villages was carried out and when thousands of civilians were killed, thousands of Muslim civilians in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday you said that the Serbs established some police of their own that had some kind of a hostile attitude towards the Muslims; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this is what is written here. It seems to be the other way around, that the Serbs had been endangered. And then, in agreement with you, they established a police through which they will be -- they will feel more secure and safer it says. In a confused situation, the SDS were catered to and a separate militia was established. On the 8th of April, 1992, that is to say that you were still there, the Executive Board of the SDA met, that is to say of your party, with the club of Assemblymen of the SDA in Bratunac headed by Dzevad Gusic, president of the SDA for Bratunac. And they passed a decision to agree to the establishment of a Serb militia, Serb police, with particular reference to some item 13 and so on and so forth. And then it says later --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. One thing at a time. The witness cannot possibly deal with this in this way. Just a moment. Let the witness answer. Now, what is alleged is that the Executive Board met on the 8th of April with the club of Assemblymen of the SDA headed by yourself. Was there such a meeting, Mr. Gusic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Such a meeting was held. And yesterday I talked about the pressures made by the SDS, and they were headed by Miroslav Deronjic to divide the police, and he said that they could wait no longer and there was direct pressure coming from President Radovan Karadzic and that we had to choose, allegedly, that we would either have peace in Bratunac or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You've told us that. So is that the meeting which is referred to, that one on the 8th of April? Yes. Very well. Yes, Mr. Milosevic. The meeting we've heard about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And then he says there was a meeting of the Municipal Assembly where the establishment of the Serb police was legalised, and he says that in honour of the agreement reached, all of those present went to the Fontana Hotel in Bratunac for a drink. This was on the 9th of April, 1992. Is that right or is that not right, Mr. Gusic?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm going to explain this to you. At this meeting of the Municipal Assembly of Bratunac, we told all the Assemblymen present, and in addition to those from Bratunac there were other citizens who were present. The hall was full. Perhaps there were some 200 persons present. The president of the Serb Democratic Party, Miroslav Deronjic, presented these requests to have the police force divided, and we explained why this police should be divided. We said that we are in a position to choose, either to have peace in the area or to have somebody from the outside come and occupy Bratunac, as was already the case in Bijeljina and Zvornik. And we put forth 13 prerequisites, conditions, in order to have this accepted, and they were the following: That a unit of the JNA --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Since time is fairly short, I must ask you to answer the question. Is it right that on the 9th of April you went to the Fontana Hotel for a drink? Did you all go there or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We from the Party of Democratic Action wanted to do our best in order to secure peace in Bratunac, and this was a move made by our side to show that we were in favour of peace and co-existence and that there was no need for anyone from the outside to come to Bratunac, which all means that yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As opposed to your testimony yesterday, is it correct then that the Serb police was established in Bratunac through legal means, that is to say at a meeting of the Municipal Assembly of Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, you cannot call this a legal meeting because the Municipal Assembly of Bratunac was not a legal organ that could have split up the police. You know that, as far as police is concerned, the republic was in charge of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So why were you engaged in this illegal activity? Now you consider it to be illegal and then you took part in it, and you were appointed head of that delegation of the SDA that proposed this, that is, for the Serbs to have a police.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was president of the Executive Board of the SDA for Bratunac and it is only natural that I headed these negotiations. At that time, we wanted to do our best only to prevent the occupation of Bratunac, that is to say something like what happened in Bijeljina. And I think that I've repeated this at least ten times and I believe that this is quite clear, more than clear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's more than clear to me and I think that it's more than clear to everybody in Bratunac. These people who were armed, the people you described, were they members of the Territorial Defence of Bratunac or of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What people do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those you saw on the 17th of April, those who were in the streets. Was that the Territorial Defence of Bratunac or the JNA?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were some military formations from Serbia. There was a certain unit of the Yugoslav People's Army there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which unit of the Yugoslav People's Army?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly which unit it was. That was there then, I mean. I know that they were present, though, because they wore JNA uniforms. I wore that kind of uniform when I did my military service in Belgrade in the neighbourhood of Vozdovac in 1984. And then when I left Bratunac on the 17th of April, after awhile when the ethnic cleansing had been carried out of all the Muslims, when all the Muslims were cleansed from Bratunac, they brought me a document. This JNA unit was under the command of Svetozar Milosevic, a colonel, and he signed that document, that proclamation on behalf of the Drina group. And he had been appointed by the General Staff of the Yugoslav People's Army from Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's not what I'm asking you. I'm asking you which unit this was, and you say that you don't know. Please, do you know, though, although you said a few minutes ago that you followed events in Bratunac and now you say that ethnic cleansing was carried out, so what do you say to the fact that all Serb villages in the municipality of Bratunac except for two were razed to the ground and their population was killed entirely except for people who managed to flee to Bratunac or to Drina -- or to Serbia across the Drina River? Is that ethnic cleansing or what do you call that?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, this piece of information is not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let the witness answer it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He says it's not correct. What more is there for him to say to that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It's being put that the Serb villages were razed. Were any of them razed at any time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the 17th of April, I left. After that, there was ethnic cleansing of all Muslims. All the Muslims from Bratunac were expelled, 21.000.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You've told us that. Forgive me, but time is short. You've told us that. Did anything happen, to your knowledge, to the Serb villages. That's the question you're being asked.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I know, only Serbs remained living in Bratunac, and during the war they engaged in certain combat operations. I was not a participant so I'm not qualified to talk about them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Are you aware of the event in Konjevic Polje on the 27th of May when columns of trucks were ambushed? These trucks were transporting bauxite. Workers were on board. No one was armed. When a group of drivers driving those trucks, who were Serbs, were killed, the vehicles damaged, an act of sabotage, traffic stopped, people killed, workers. They were not soldiers or I don't know who, any kind of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. politicians. They were simply workers, drivers driving truckloads of bauxite.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that but I think it is not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. So you think it's not true. I have here a list of the names of people who were killed.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will tell you now you will have more witnesses who are more qualified to talk about that, and I would like to ask you to discuss that matter with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I can't talk to the people who were killed, but I can tell you that the attack was carried out upon orders of Ferid Fodzic, whose father's name is Avdo. And the actual perpetrators were Semsudin Salihovic, Munib Alic, Meho --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You're not going to get away with this. The witness knows nothing about it. If you want to call your evidence about the incident as alleged, you can do so but you can't put it to the witness. In fact, you've got one minute left, so that's time for two questions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a lot of questions left, Mr. May.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that on the 29th of May, in the village of Sandici on the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje road, an ambush set by these non-existent forces, according to you, ten policemen were killed? Is that true?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. So is it true that in an attack on the Serbian village of Gornji Magasici in Bratunac municipality on the 25th of June, 1992, 12 civilians were killed, Serbs?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the information is not true. I wasn't there at that time so I'm unable to comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You've had your time now, ample time. Yes, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Questioned by Mr. Tapuskovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Gusic, is it true that you attended a meeting with Serbs, you yourself, and that at that meeting you suggested to your Serb neighbours that joint guards be formed to protect each other? Would you tell us who did you need to protect yourself against together with the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, we had received certain information that military formations from Serbia and the JNA would occupy Bratunac. We had that information based on the facts that this had already happened in Bijeljina and Zvornik. So we tried, with our Serb neighbours, to discuss the matter, saying that we were neighbours, that we had been living together for many years, that we knew each other very well, and that we should remain on good terms regardless of the times that were coming, and that we should jointly organise these guards in the streets and areas where people were living together, co-existing multi-ethnically, and that was the reason why I had that conversation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if I understood you correctly, you were talking to Serbs, that the Serbs protect themselves against the Serbs and the JNA.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from the Serbs coming from Serbia and the JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Also, at a meeting with representatives of the JNA, you went there to raise a number of questions, among others why they were hastening into war; was that right?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was a meeting with the leadership of the Serbian Democratic Party, and the leadership of the SDA was present as well as prominent citizens from Bratunac, both Serbs and Muslims. There were about 60 or 70 people attending, and then we asked the Serbs why they were rushing into war, why were people being trained militarily, and why was the JNA and the SDS training people in the village of Vranesevici while the barrels of guns were turned towards inhabited areas in Bratunac, why we needed that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You already explained that when you were questioned during the examination-in-chief. I'm asking you, did you know at the end of 1991 and the beginning of 1992 what had happened in Croatia and Slovenia?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we had information about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And didn't you know that certain things had already happened over there which had increased tension between the peoples living in those areas?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We knew about that, but the problem of the Muslim people specifically was that they trusted their Serb neighbours. They had lived together for a long time on good terms. And the Muslim people in Bratunac could not imagine that such a situation would occur. There were individual Muslims who were aware of what was happening and who tried to open the eyes of the others as to what was about to happen, but generally speaking, the Muslims trusted their Serb neighbours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, would you please look at Exhibit 436, tab 1. You will find there the document in which the witness gave his personal data, and also there's a part about his career. So would you please look at that document in the Serbian language. It has been signed by Mr. Gusic on the 2nd of May, 2003. And now I would like to ask him something in connection with the second paragraph that has been translated into English where there is talk of his working experience.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic, you said here to the Prosecutors the other day that on the 17th of April, 1992, you left Bratunac. You were in Gradacac, and you returned about a month later; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you say later, after that, that a month after the 17th of April, that is in May, you joined a unit of the army of BiH consisting of about 400 combatants as a regular soldier; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The commander of this unit was Nurif Rizvanovic. The unit spent a month in Banovic municipality close to Tuzla and then later you joined the troops of the BH army in Bratunac and Srebrenica. Is that right? Does that mean that a month after the 17th of April this unit numbered 400 combatants and all of them were armed? Is that true?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that the commander Nurif Rizvanovic had, out of the expelled Muslims after the cleansing of Bratunac municipality, he rallied a sufficient number of combatants, about 400 of them, who were ready to return to a part of the free territory of the municipality, that is Konjevic Polje and Srebrenica, and those 400 fighters managed to pass between the lines and to return into that encirclement together with the commander Nurif Rizvanovic who succeeded in arming all 400 fighters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But weren't you a member of that unit and weren't you armed?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spent a month in that unit and then I needed to go to Croatia where my family was. In the meantime, while I was in Croatia, this unit passed between the lines and entered a part of Bratunac municipality territory that is Konjevic Polje and Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but it says here that you returned to Tuzla and joined the Bratunac unit under the command of the 2nd Tuzla Corps. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you spent some time there from the end of 1992 to the beginning of 1993 as a part of that armed military unit.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it true, Mr. Gusic, that during that time you were assistant commander for morality of commander Becir Mekanic? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does a person who is responsible for morale in a unit actually do?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as my duties as assistant commander for moral guidance is concerned, they consist of the following: My duty was to regularly brief the combatants about all events on the front within Bosnia and Herzegovina, also to inform them about all important political developments in Bosnia and Herzegovina and in the world. A second part of my duties was to work on preparing the combatants for performing their duties responsibly. A third part of my duties was to make it possible for combatants to freely practice their faith and to engage in religious rights. And a fourth part of my duties was, together with the logistics department, to ensure for the combatants cigarettes, newspapers, hygienic material, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, as from May 1992 up to 1993, you were continuously a member of the armed units of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, one more question. The last sentence says: "I personally did not see any atrocities." That's what you said.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where is this sentence?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The last sentence of your statement of the 15th of April. You say, "I personally did not eyewitness any atrocities." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I please say which context?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You later on heard about things. It is the last sentence of your statement.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the statement of the 15th of April, 1999?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That probably refers to the date of the 17th of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I will find the sentence for you.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, you read the sentence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you like to read it for yourself, please.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is very important to read this sentence: "That is how I escaped the horrors that I learnt later happened in Bratunac and surrounding villages." This is a reference to ethnic cleansing. So I was not a witness to any of the atrocities myself, but I am aware of what took place there as naturally they will have been discussed on many occasions subsequently.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: A couple matters, Your Honour. Re-examined by Mr. Nice:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were asked about paragraph 28 of the summary, that is the visit of MUP officials Koljevic, Galic, and others and about the events associated with that visit. You told us about an assertion that the investigation into events would not take place. Do you remember? Ganic said the perpetrators would be caught. Koljevic travelled to the location and spoke to a larger gathering of Serbs. What was it that Koljevic said?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was agreed -- Mr. Koljevic and Mr. Ganic first came to see the president of the municipality of Bratunac, and it was agreed that two major rallies be held, one in Bratunac and another in Kravica. In Bratunac, it should have been a multi-ethnic rally that both of them addressed to tell the people that an investigation would be carried out and that the perpetrators of the killing that occurred in Kravica would be discovered and treated and punished in accordance with the law. And Messrs. Koljevic and Ganic were to go to Kravica together to address the Serb peoples with the same message and with the same promises. Mr. Koljevic, on his own initiative, that is without the other Presidency member, Mr. Ganic, went to Kravica and spoke to the Serb people in Kravica and told them on that occasion not to worry, that no investigation would be initiated in connection with those killings. Also at the same time, I had occasion to hear Radovan Karadzic on the radio who said to the Serb people that the MUP of Bosnia and Herzegovina would not carry out an investigation into that matter and that he was guaranteeing that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You spoke on a couple of occasions about the movement of some Serbs away from the area of Bratunac. This is dealt with at paragraphs 31 and 46 of the summary. Was that a genuine movement or was there anything about it that you doubted as to its genuineness?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had two cases in the few months prior to the 17th of April when a certain number of Serbs moved out of Bratunac. These were mostly elderly people, women, and children. This happened on two occasions, the first time after this killing carried out by the Serbs in Kravica when they killed two Muslims and wounded another two. In those days, the Serbs had no reason to move out of Bratunac. The second alleged reason that they gave, regardless of the fact that they had liquidated those Bosniaks, they claimed that they were in danger. And this was at the beginning of April, I think it was the 1st of April when, on the 30th of March, Serb military units entered Bijeljina and occupied Bijeljina and committed certain atrocities over there so that in the first days of April, again allegedly being in danger, these Serb families started moving out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have the drift of your answers to both -- your explanation of for both departures. If the explanation for the departure as given by the Serbs was not genuine, what, as you could you calculate or see, was the real reason for these departures?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can claim with certainty that the Serbs had no justifiable reason to move out. The real reason for them leaving could be described in a few sentences. It was designed to achieve several effects. First, additional homogenisation of the Serb people. Second, to show to the Serbs in Serbia, specifically in Ljubovija, that the Serbs in Bratunac in Bosnia and Herzegovina were in jeopardy and that Mother Serbia headed by the accused, Slobodan Milosevic, needed to protect them. And a third and perhaps most important matter, it was a kind of practice so that the Serbian people would be easily placed under the unified command of the Yugoslav People's Army and the SDS so as to occupy Bratunac, as happened on the 17th of April, as easily as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that's all I'll ask of this witness in re-examination, given the time constraints and the very detailed nature of his answers earlier and indeed to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic, that concludes your evidence. Thank you for coming to the International Tribunal to give it. You are now free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: There are some procedural matters to deal with before the next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And I have some to raise as well, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let me deal with -- there are some rulings which I want to give. There's one ruling which will require something to go to the interpreters but let me deal with the other matters first. The first is protective measures for the next witness, B-1461. We have a motion of the 5th of May. We are going to grant it in the terms asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would just ask that the usher inform the witness as I will not have an opportunity before he comes, that the protections he asked for has been afforded by the court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We must make sure that that message is passed on to him since nobody's here. The next matter is a purely procedural matter, and it's this: That Judge Kwon is required to be absent on Tribunal business in June, and the Trial Chamber will sit in his absence composed of Judge Robinson and myself. That is between Monday the 16th and Thursday the 19th of June. The two Judges will sit pursuant to Rule 15 bis of the Rules. And the formal order will be made today. Don't stand for this, please, Mr. Nice. I'm going to read out a ruling which I hope the interpreters now have concerning -- the final ruling it is on the Croatia Rule 92 bis witnesses. It relates to the following: Witness C-1086, 1089, 1162, 1175, 1185, 1215, 1238, 1055, 1136, 1191. All the witnesses deal with events about which evidence has been given, and they are cumulative in the sense of the ruling of the 7th of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. April, that is, alleged attacks or killings by the JNA or paramilitary forces. The statements will be admitted under Rule 92 bis. Apart from two witnesses, C-1089 and 1162, all concern or mention the activities and conduct of the JNA about which the accused has raised an issue for the Trial Chamber to determine. Therefore, apart from these two, all the witnesses are required to attend for cross-examination. The statements of C-1089 and 1162 concern arrests and detention by Arkan's men. It has not been disputed that such arrests and detention took place, and no crucial issue turns on the evidence of these two witnesses. Accordingly, their statements will be admitted without cross-examination. The final matter I want to raise is this: Mr. Nice, it concerns your application for more time. We've had your motion, and we've had a response or observation by the amici. It may be helpful, since we're not sitting next week, to schedule a procedural hearing on it, on the motion, this week.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: A point of three points to which I was coming. We are filing a very short reply to the document of the amici today, I hope by lunch-time. There may be time this week for procedural argument even if we deal with the witnesses who are listed for this week, because one of them is going to be postponed, and I'm coming to that in a second --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I think we should have it this week since we're not sitting the next week so we can consider the matter next week.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: It may be that I won't be able to be here on Friday, or I shouldn't be here on Friday, so Thursday might be a possibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thursday, Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let us schedule it for Thursday. Find a convenient -- maybe the last session or something of the sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The two other matters are these: The propaganda expert, Mr. de la Brosse, is listed for this week. He has come with a number of documents that will require translation for the French and for that reason and indeed for possibly some others, I think it is desirable that he should be put back until probably the beginning of the week following the break. So that the list of witnesses will be as is but without Mr. de la Brosse, and that indeed will probably free up enough time for hearing on Thursday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: So we can remove Mr. de la Brosse from the list. I see we've got three fairly substantial witnesses anyway before we were due to reach him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes. Although of course, we're going to apply or seek to apply the provisions of 92 bis to abbreviate the evidence in chief of at least I think two of them, or certainly of one. But that's the position, yes, please. And the last and separate procedural matter is this: The Chamber will recall the 54 bis application, at the end of which a decision was made with a two-month time limit on it. That two calendar month time limit expires on Saturday. We are currently assessing what quantity of materials, if any, have been provided in that two-month period, and I -- on the basis of the quantity of materials supplied, we will certainly need a further hearing. I understand that documents are being prepared by the other party to that application now, and I'm not sure, because I simply don't know, whether that is simply a report or whether it's a report with documentation being provided right at the end of the two-month period, which would be less helpful and less appropriate than to have provided it as soon as it became available. But one way or another, we would like to arrange for a very early return date to that application because of the pressures of time and the absolute need we now have to secure documentation of the kind listed in the original application, and would ask the Chamber to consider having a hearing in the beginning of the week after the break, if that's possible. We hope to file a report ourselves, whether with or without sight of whatever the respondents to that application are preparing this week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Obviously we'll consider that when the matter is reported to us. If you could give as full a report as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: If we get our document in before the weekend, even if the respondents exercise their right to put things right up to the deadline, Friday afternoon or whatever it may be - or next Monday, I suppose - we hope that our document will assist in the need for an early return date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome will take the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Call the next witness. The legal officer, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Let the witness take the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you'd like to take a seat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, as a preliminary matter, Witness B-1461 will give his entire testimony in open session. He will be referring to sexual crimes against a number of victims. I will not elicit those names during my examination of him, but should they become relevant or should anyone seek to ask the identity, I would ask that the identities of those victims be taken in closed session. Examined by Mr. Groome:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: B-1461, I would ask you to take a look at this piece of paper. And if it could please be assigned an exhibit number, the pseudonym sheet.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Prosecution Exhibit 437 under seal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd ask you to take a look at the name printed on the top of that sheet. Is that your name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the purposes of protecting your identity, I will refer to you as B-1461 during the course of my questions to you. Sir, I'd ask you to begin your testimony today by telling us from where -- where were you born and where did you grow up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: I was born in the Zvornik municipality, and the place is called Divic, where I went to school and worked and lived until the beginning of the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give us some idea regarding the size of the village of Divic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: The village had a population of -- that is to say about 300 houses and approximately two and a half thousand inhabitants. It's a small place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: I'm a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you -- was there a predominant ethnic group that lived in the village of Divic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: The majority were Muslims. One Serbian family, and five from mixed marriages with Muslims, that were ethnic Serbs married to Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to ask you some questions about the geography of Zvornik. Would I be correct in saying that the town of Zvornik itself lies on the western bank of the Drina River?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is the town of Zvornik and in fact all of Zvornik municipality in the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, or at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the town of Mali Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe to the Chamber where Mali Zvornik is with respect to Zvornik itself.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: Mali Zvornik is located in the Republic of Serbia, right up on the border with Bosnia-Herzegovina, across the Drina River.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would it be fair to say that Mali Zvornik lies directly across -- Mali Zvornik in Serbia lies directly across from Zvornik in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are there ways to cross the Drina between Zvornik and Mali Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: Yes; across the bridges.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many bridges connect those two different municipalities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: In the municipality of Zvornik, three bridges.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in 19 -- the winter and spring of 1992, were there border controls on those bridges?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: Yes, prior to the beginning of the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could I ask you to describe, where is Divic with respect to the town of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: Divic is 2.5 kilometres from the town of Zvornik, in the direction of Sarajevo, on the Sarajevo road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how far away is the village of Divic from the River Drina itself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: Well, it lies on the Drina River, on the banks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can somebody in the village of Divic look across the Drina and into Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: Yes, with boats.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, do you think we can get the year of his birth --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you please tell us the year of your birth.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: My date of birth. Do you want the year or the --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Simply the year.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I think there was some misunderstanding or mistranslation of my last question. My question to you was, can you see across, not necessarily cross the river, but can you see across into Serbia from the village of Divic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: Yes, you can see it, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to draw your attention to the spring of 1992, more specifically March of 1992. Did you notice anything unusual occurring in Serbia across from your village of Divic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: Yes, I did notice something. I noticed artillery weapons that had been positioned on the opposite side of the river.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give us some idea about the quantity and size of these weapons that you could see.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: There were anti-aircraft armoured vehicles and somewhat fewer tanks. That was to begin with. Later on, there were others too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And approximately how many tanks did you see in March of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: About ten.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were the artillery and tanks, were they directed in any particular direction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: All the barrels were directed towards the Bosnian side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, prior to you seeing this build-up or this placement of artillery and tanks in Serbia, did -- was there any violence that you were aware of in your village or in the surrounding area to your village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: No, there wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the people of Divic do anything in response to seeing these weapons across the river?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a rally in early April 1992 in the village of Divic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: The rally was held in the town of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you attend that rally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the purpose of that rally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: The purpose of the rally was for people to continue their normal lives, living the way they had before and to avoid a war or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that rally, did the people of Divic form a Crisis Staff and begin to make some preparations for the defence of their village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: When they noticed the barricades and when they felt that a war would take place, they began to organise themselves and set up a Crisis Staff in the village of Divic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe what if any weapons this Crisis Staff or the people who had prepared to defend themselves in Divic had.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: In the Crisis Staff, there was about 18 to 20 rifles. Some were privately owned, some were obtained from the local community or municipality, or I don't know how it came about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the location named Kula Grad in the municipality of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you assist the Chamber by describing where Kula Grad is with respect to the town of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: Kula Grad is situated on an elevation above the town of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is Kula Grad in Serbia or in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: In Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you saw Kula Grad being shelled?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your best recollection of the time period during which Kula Grad was shelled?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: The tanks fired shells on Kula Grad from the Serb side around the hydroelectric power plant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you assist the Chamber in giving the date or the dates to the best of your recollection when this occurred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: It occurred in April, after the fall of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you yourself see the shells coming from Serbia and hitting Kula Grad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Around this same period did you see something in the Drina that indicated to you that there were -- there was violence elsewhere in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: Yes. We noticed some corpses flowing down the Drina River. There were some dead people and some livestock, things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you approximate the number of corpses that you yourself observed floating down the Drina River.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number, but I think that we reported them, and several of them turned up to take the people away. I don't know the exact number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the name Marko Pavlovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know this person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: I didn't know him before, but he used to come to Divic, to the Crisis Staff for negotiations, and he asked that the weapons be handed over. The first time he came was with a man who had an agreement with someone from Serbia to go and buy some cigarettes, and the Serb army arrested him, brought him in, and he came with Marko Pavlovic. And from the Crisis Staff, I learnt his name, that his name was in fact Marko Pavlovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many times did you see this person Marko Pavlovic in the village of Divic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: Twice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you approximate the times or the dates when you saw Marko Pavlovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: The last time was on the 22nd of May -- the 22nd of April, the 18th of April, that kind of thing. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've testified that he asked that weapons be handed over. Did the people of Divic hand over weapons to Marko Pavlovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: No. First of all, they asked him to give us some sort of guarantee, and he said that he could sign the guarantee but it was a worthless piece of paper as far as we were concerned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened in response to the refusal of the people of Divic to turn over their weapons to Marko Pavlovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: How do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened after this refusal? Did anything happen after the people of Divic refused to hand over their weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: Nothing special.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time when the village of Divic came under attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When, to the best of your recollection, did that occur?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: That was sometime around the 26th of April, after the fall of Kula Grad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I ask you, what -- how did the attack begin? What was the first thing that you recall happening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: That morning when the attack on Divic started, they asked from across the River Drina, that is on the Serbian side, they asked the inhabitants of Divic to surrender their weapons. They said they didn't have any more confidence in Kula Grad, and we were left on our own.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: And after that, the first attack followed from the Serb side, started from the Serb side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please describe specifically what occurred during the course of that attack.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: The beginning of the attack was at around 10.00, roughly, and it went on for two hours. After that, there was a pause, a lull, and then the attack continued for about an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The witness will have to clarify what he means by that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you use the word "attack," can you please be specific about people involved, types of equipment involved. What exactly did you mean when you used the word "attack"? What are your specific observations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: Well, I think the attack or, rather, the attack was launched from the Serbian side with all possible means available, and this refers to artillery, and the attack was on our place, Divic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "artillery," did shells hit the town or village of Divic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you able to see from where they were fired?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: I didn't see all of it, but I did see the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is that a convenient place to pause, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. We will adjourn now. Witness B-1461, we're going to adjourn now for 20 minutes. During the adjournment and any others which there may be while you're giving evidence, don't speak to anybody about it until it's over, and don't let anybody speak to you about it, and that does include the members of the Prosecution team. So don't speak to anybody about your evidence while you're giving it. Could you be back, please, in 20 minutes. We will adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: B-1461, we finished just before the break with you describing your observations about what was occurring on the Serbian side of the river. Could you please describe what your observations were with respect to the attack occurring in the village itself.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: Well, as I've already said, this attack was carried out by this equipment of theirs or, rather, their artillery which was on the other side of the Drina, rather in Serbia. There were snipers and light weapons, and then I noticed later a personnel carrier which was moving along the other side of the Drina River, that is to say in Serbia, and which was coming close to our town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time when armed people actually entered the village of Divic itself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: Not on that day, but they came the following morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you describe approximately how many armed people entered the village the following morning.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but I think there was one unit that came and that expelled people from their homes and ordered them to go towards the hotel which was towards the end of our town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is the name of that hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: Vidikovac Hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The armed people that you saw in your village, could you describe what they were wearing.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: They were in camouflage uniforms. I don't remember the insignia they had. I think it was the so-called tricolour flag. I don't know whether it's the flag of Serbia, I can't say exactly. And they all carried automatic weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise any -- well, let me ask you this first: The people -- the armed people that came into the town, were their faces covered or obstructed in any way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: No, they weren't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of these people as being from the area of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1461
utterances.text: No, I didn't recognise them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
